title: The KV-Surgeon: Compensation-Aware Offline KV-Cache Compaction
summary: Replaces per-entry independent scoring for KV-cache eviction (e.g., attention matching) with a calibration-data-driven quadratic surrogate that jointly selects removals and compensates remaining entries, accounting for softmax renormalization. Cost is a one-time offline compaction pass with calibration data per fixed context, plus the memory of retaining a small calibration set; the compacted cache then reduces per-query memory and compute on repeated queries. It can fail when the queried context is not fixed and reused (no amortization of the offline cost), when calibration data is unrepresentative of production queries, or when compaction ratios are pushed beyond the validated operating points.
rationale: The method directly fits constrained single-GPU inference of 4B-30B models and repeated fixed-context workloads, but the gain depends on having stable contexts and suitable calibration data, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces per-entry independent scoring for KV-cache eviction (e.g., attention matching) with a calibration-data-driven quadratic surrogate that jointly selects removals and compensates remaining entries, accounting for softmax renormalization. Cost is a one-time offline compaction pass with calibration data per fixed context, plus the memory of retaining a small calibration set; the compacted cache then reduces per-query memory and compute on repeated queries. It can fail when the queried context is not fixed and reused (no amortization of the offline cost), when calibration data is unrepresentative of production queries, or when compaction ratios are pushed beyond the validated operating points.

At 50x compaction, improves QA accuracy by up to four points over attention matching (prior SOTA) at comparable cost; a faster variant also exceeds SOTA at two fifths of its cost, evaluated on models from 4B to 30B parameters.
